summary: Apply GIS, satellite data, and risk analysis to resilient urban planning. Build practical maps, scenarios, and investment briefs. Enrol today.
lede: Risk-based urban planning and infrastructure resilience with GIS connects satellite imagery, municipal data, spatial analysis, and investment decisions. You will learn to map flood and heat exposure, identify vulnerable people and assets, examine infrastructure dependencies, and assess how land-use changes may affect future risk. Practise QGIS and ArcGIS Pro workflows, work with Sentinel-1, Sentinel-2, Landsat, and elevation data, and create exposure maps, risk registers, priority matrices, planning briefs, and a risk-based dashboard. You will also compare urban growth scenarios with suitability analysis and an introductory SLEUTH model while interpreting flood extent outputs conceptually with HEC-RAS.
audienceIntro: This course is designed for professionals who use maps, infrastructure data, and hazard evidence to shape urban investment and resilience decisions. It suits beginner-to-intermediate geospatial practitioners who can work with basic spatial data and want stronger planning and risk-analysis outputs.
modules: Exposure Mapping with GIS and Remote Sensing
Urban Hazard Measurement and Data Quality
GIS and Remote Sensing for Urban Planning Scenarios
prerequisites: You should have basic GIS literacy, including map navigation, layer management, attribute-table use, and simple spatial queries. Familiarity with urban planning, infrastructure services, climate hazards, or disaster risk management will help, but advanced remote sensing or hydrodynamic modelling experience is not required. No coding or programming is required for completion. Advanced subjects such as Google Earth Engine, AI-assisted classification, and SLEUTH are taught at conceptual awareness and operational application levels, while QGIS-based mapping and scenario analysis receive hands-on practice.
